title: What If Planes Ran on Nuclear Reactors? The US Flew One 47 Times

scenes.text: What if planes ran on nuclear reactors? The US built one, and flew it with the reactor running.
The NB-36H, a giant Cold War bomber with a one-megawatt reactor in its bomb bay.
From 1955 to 1957 it flew 47 times, 215 hours in the air. The reactor ran for 89 of them.
To protect the five crew, the cockpit was a capsule of lead and rubber weighing about eleven tons.
On every flight a second plane full of armed Marines followed, ready to parachute in and seal off a crash site.
The reactor never powered the engines. In 1961 Kennedy cancelled it after about a billion dollars. Grounded by the weight of its own shield.

description:
What if planes ran on nuclear reactors? The United States tested the idea for real: the Convair NB-36H flew 47 times between 1955 and 1957 with a 1 megawatt reactor on board, running for 89 of its 215 flight hours.
The crew sat inside an 11 ton capsule of lead and rubber, a plane of armed Marines followed to secure any crash site, and the reactor never actually drove the engines. President Kennedy cancelled the program in 1961 after about 1 billion dollars.
What should we run through next?
